realism_constraints: No advanced forensic DNA analysis available
Chemical poisons and toxins known but detection limited to chemical tests
Film technology limited to black-and-white silent films with physical negatives
location: Tarrytown and New York City, USA
institution: District Attorney's Office of Westchester County and Manton Pictures studio
crime_subtype: needle poisoned with snake venom hidden in curtains

cast.name: Lawrence Millard
cast.role_archetype: author and scenario writer, jealous ex-husband
opportunity_channels: access to studio and Phelps's house

surface_summary: Stella Lamar, a popular film star, suddenly collapses and dies during filming at a country house. The director Werner later dies mysteriously during a banquet scene. Suspicion falls on multiple people connected to the film company, with mysterious poisons and sabotage complicating the case.
accepted_facts: Stella Lamar died suddenly during filming in the library at Emery Phelps's house.
A tiny scratch on Stella's arm was the cause of death.
Stanley Werner, the director, died from poisoning during a banquet scene.
An incendiary fire destroyed the film negatives in the studio vault.
inferred_conclusions: Werner was the murderer and drug addict responsible for the deaths.
Merle Shirley was guilty due to his anger and jealousy.
Lloyd Manton was deliberately wrecking the company and responsible for the murders.
mechanism_description: Lawrence Millard poisoned Stella Lamar by placing a needle coated with snake venom in the library curtains, which pricked her arm during filming. He inoculated himself with antivenin to avoid death from the venom. To silence the director Werner, who suspected him, Millard poisoned him with botulin toxin in a glass of wine during a banquet scene. Millard also attempted to destroy evidence by setting fire to the film vault.
delivery_path: Millard prepared a hypodermic needle coated with rattlesnake venom.
He inserted the needle into the heavy silk curtains in the library at a height and position calculated to prick Stella's arm when she moved the curtains during filming.
Stella was pricked by the needle during the scene and died from the venom.
Millard inoculated himself with antivenin serum to protect against accidental poisoning.
Werner discovered clues implicating Millard and was poisoned with botulin toxin in his wine glass during a banquet scene.
Millard planted misleading evidence such as a cigarette case and ampulla to implicate others.
Millard set fire to the film vault to destroy incriminating negatives.
outcome_result: Lawrence Millard is exposed as the murderer through scientific evidence and arrested.

false_assumption.statement: Stanley Werner, the nervous drug-addicted director, was the murderer.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Werner was nervous, had access to the victim, and possessed hypodermic needles and drugs, which suggested capability and opportunity. His erratic behavior and drug addiction made him a plausible suspect.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It hides the fact that Werner was actually a victim who discovered the murderer and was poisoned to silence him. His drug use was unrelated to the murders.

supporting_points: Werner was nervous and acted suspiciously during questioning.
He had hypodermic needles and was a known drug addict.
He was present at the scenes of the crimes and had opportunity.
He was the second man seen at the house break-in.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Werner was himself poisoned with a different toxin and was trying to expose the real murderer.

red_herrings.description: Werner's drug addiction and possession of hypodermic needles suggested guilt.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Werner was a drug addict but was innocent of murder; he was a victim and tried to uncover the truth.

red_herrings.description: Lloyd Manton's financial troubles and business schemes suggested he might have motive to kill.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Manton was involved in financial schemes but had no direct involvement in the murders; his behavior was business-driven, not criminal.

closed_circle.rationale: All were present at the studio or house, had possible motives or opportunity, and were investigated thoroughly, forming a closed circle of suspects.

time_anchors: Time of Stella's death during filming of scene 13
Time of Werner's death during banquet scene
Time of fire in film vault four days after Stella's death
Time of attempted murder on Shirley during ballroom scene
time_windows: Between arrival at Phelps's house and filming of scene 13

inference_path.observation: Tiny scratch on Stella Lamar's arm with faint blood and poison stains on curtains
inference_path.correction: The scratch was caused by a needle hidden in the curtains, not a natural cause
required_evidence: Piece of heavy silk cut from portieres with two microscopic holes and blood stains
Microscopic examination of the scratch on Stella's arm

inference_path.observation: Blood spots on towel found in studio washroom with antivenin traces
inference_path.correction: The towel was used to wipe a needle after inoculation with antivenin
inference_path.effect: Links suspect to needle and poison
required_evidence: Chemical analysis of towel spots showing antivenin

inference_path.observation: Werner died suddenly with symptoms of food poisoning
inference_path.correction: Werner was poisoned with botulin toxin in his wine glass
required_evidence: Broken stem of wine glass with toxin residue
Film footage of banquet scene showing Werner drinking wine

inference_path.observation: Fire destroyed film negatives in vault
inference_path.correction: Fire was incendiary, caused by phosphorus bomb to destroy evidence
inference_path.effect: Attempt to cover up murder evidence
required_evidence: Chemical analysis of fire cause and phosphorus residues
Recovered piece of negative film showing snake venom scenes

inference_path.observation: Shirley collapsed during ballroom scene after drinking poison
inference_path.correction: Attempted murder with belladonna to simulate suicide
inference_path.effect: Third attempt on life linked to murders
required_evidence: Film footage of Shirley drinking poison

inference_path.observation: Fibers of impregnated towel found on suspect's fingernail files and pocket knives
inference_path.correction: Suspect handled the towel impregnated with chemical and itching salve
inference_path.effect: Direct evidence linking suspect to towel and crime
required_evidence: Microscopic examination of fingernail files and knives

inference_path.observation: Blood samples from suspects show presence of antivenin in one individual
inference_path.correction: That individual inoculated himself against snake venom
required_evidence: Blood smear analysis showing antivenin presence
Matching blood type to blood on portieres

discriminating_test.design: Project the film scenes of Stella Lamar's death, Werner's poisoning, and Shirley's attempted poisoning to all suspects. Observe reactions and compare with scientific evidence from blood and fiber analysis to identify the guilty party.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals the calculated method of murder and the identity of the murderer through scientific proof and behavioral reactions.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Identification of the suspect whose blood matches the evidence and who reacts to the projection of the incriminating scenes.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the crime scenes, the tiny scratch, the presence of the needle in the curtains, the chemical analysis of the towel and blood, and the motives and opportunities of all suspects. The scientific detective's reasoning is presented clearly, allowing the reader to deduce the murderer by connecting the clues about the needle, venom, antivenin, and the staged poisonings. The false suspicion of Werner is also clearly shown and refuted.
